To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies were detected in COVID-19 recovered patients from 10-15 days after the onset of illness, and remained thereafter, (2) the neutralization titers of SARS-CoV2 were variable among these patients, and (3) neutralization titers were positively correlated with age, blood CRP, but negatively correlated with lymphocyte count, suggesting the interplay between host immune response and virus in COVID-19.
SARS CoV NAbs are not able to cross reactive with COVID 19 virus, and the levels of SARS Co 2 NAbs in recovered patients are variable.
SARS CoV NAbs are not cross reactive with S2 CoV 2, the titers of SARS Co V 2 specific NAb among these COVID 19 patients were variable, and there were ten patients who were unable to produce NAb.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of drugs, called "neutralizing antibodies", which have the ability to block the entry of the virus into the cells.
the development of an in vitro assay for the detection of neutralizing antibodies against the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which is the cause of COVID-19.
the development and application of a safe and sensitive assay for the detection of SARS CoVs neutralizing antibodies in plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NAb titers are associated with the age and the severity of the COVID 19 patients.
there are a wide range of NAb titres among recovered COVID 19 patient, which may have important implications for the development of an effective vaccine.
the SARS-CoV-2 virus has a wide range of symptoms that can be fatal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that SARS CoV-2 specific neutralizing antibodies were detected from day 10-15 after the onset in COVID-19 patients.
we have developed an assay to measure the SARS CoV2 neutralizing antibody in plasma.
the neutralization assay we used was safe and sensitive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the titers of SARS Co V 2 specific NA bs were variable in COVID 19 patients and correlated with the age and the immune status of patients.
there are variations in the neutralizing antibody responses to the SARS CoV2 coronavirus in COVID 19 recovered mild symptomatic patients.
